- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) or negative, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to compensate for bearish sentiment bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged flat or downward trend; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to avoid overshoot.
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model may underestimate rebound; add 2–5% upward bias in next forecast to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.4–0.7), model often underestimates upward momentum; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with sentiment-driven expectations.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period price increases (especially after mid-forecast); apply a 2–5% upward adjustment in final 5–7 days to capture tail-end momentum.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often fails to react quickly; delay forecast adjustment until sentiment stabilizes or add 1–2% lagged momentum to next forecast.
